records.Concise description: Rutherford Chang’s conceptual Ordinals work documenting 10,000 U.S. copper cents and linking the digital inscriptions to a physical mass of copper.
records.Deeper researched summary: CENTS extends Chang’s long-running interest in monetary objects into Bitcoin. The project documented individual copper cents as inscriptions and connected them conceptually to a physical copper block weighing roughly 69 pounds. It is a finite art project rather than an actively expanding protocol or community product.
records.Launch / history: Presented in the 2023–2024 Ordinals art period through Sovrn/related exhibition channels as a 10,000-cent conceptual work.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: CENTS bridges physical money, material value, archival documentation, and Bitcoin inscription provenance in a way that broadens Ordinals beyond PFP culture.
records.Verification basis: Artist/gallery presentation plus current indexer visibility.
Research notes / uncertainties: Conceptual project materials describe 10,000 cents; some current indexers expose a slightly smaller indexed count (~9,993). Do not publish an indexed supply until reconciled.

records.Concise description: A 10,000-piece frog PFP collection launched as a free mint in March 2023 and widely recognized as an early large Ordinals collection.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitcoin Frogs launched very early in the 10k collection era and used a free-mint model. The official site states that 10,000 Frogs were created and no more will be made. Although the mint is finite, the official project account and founder-identifying channels continued active communication into 2026, including a third-anniversary site refresh. MSC therefore classifies Bitcoin Frogs as ACTIVE: finite supply does not by itself make a project historical when ongoing project/community operation is verified.
Creators / founders: Anonymous / pseudonymous team; official public identity not fully verified
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: It became one of the earliest widely recognized 10k Ordinals PFP communities and helped normalize large free-mint collections on Bitcoin.
records.Verification basis: Current official site plus current 2026 project/founder communications.
Research notes / uncertainties: Finite mint status does not imply HISTORICAL status while verified project/community operation continues.
Secondary-market trading is not used as the basis for ACTIVE status.

records.Concise description: A 3,333-piece Taproot Wizards collection built around evolving inscriptions and the campaign to restore OP_CAT to Bitcoin.
records.Deeper researched summary: Quantum Cats uses evolving inscription techniques and a cat visual language to support Taproot Wizards’ OP_CAT advocacy. The current Taproot Wizards portal lists 3,333 cats. The project is technically/culturally important because it ties changing on-chain art states to an explicit Bitcoin scripting debate, but the collection’s advocacy should not be confused with OP_CAT activation in Bitcoin itself.
Creators / founders: Udi Wertheimer and Eric Wall — Taproot Wizards co-founders
records.Launch / history: Launched in early 2024 and continued evolving alongside Taproot Wizards’ OP_CAT advocacy and ecosystem programs.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: Quantum Cats made evolving inscriptions and Bitcoin opcode advocacy visible to a broad collector audience.
records.Verification basis: Current official Quantum Cats site and Taproot Wizards portal.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not imply OP_CAT is a currently activated consensus feature based on project messaging alone.

records.Concise description: An Ordinals-era continuation of the 2013 'Magic Internet Money' Bitcoin Wizard meme originally created by Mavensbot.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitcoin Wizards directly connects contemporary Ordinals culture to one of Bitcoin’s best-known early internet memes. Official project material credits Mavensbot with the original 2013 wizard artwork and documents its later inscription-era community. This is distinct from Taproot Wizards and The Wizards of Ord, which are separate projects despite similar names.
Creators / founders: Mavensbot — original 2013 Magic Internet Money artist
records.Launch / history: The original Bitcoin Wizard meme dates to 2013; an Ordinals-native Bitcoin Wizards project/community formed in 2023 and remains active.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: It is an unusually direct bridge between pre-Ordinals Bitcoin internet culture and inscription-era collecting.
Important technical or cultural characte: Distinct from Taproot Wizards and The Wizards of Ord

Official sources.label: Magic Internet Money official project site

records.Verification basis: Current official Bitcoin Wizard and related first-party project sites.
Research notes / uncertainties: Name collision risk is high; UI should clearly distinguish Bitcoin Wizards, Taproot Wizards, and The Wizards of Ord.
